back: The long-term direction (trajectory) of an organization. Key words: long-term, direction, organization.
Purposive social collections of controlled resources, building exchange relations and interacting with other entities, and developing strategies for reaching objectives.
Why = purpose (mission, vision, values, objectives). Where = industry & scope: customers, geography, activities → corporate strategy. How = resources & capabilities → business strategy.
Corporate (scope, diversification, resource allocation) · Business (how to compete in a market) · Functional (implementation by the functions). Need strategic integration.
OE = same activities done better → productivity frontier, imitated quickly → competitive convergence. Strategy = different activities or different ways.
Variety-based (subset of products, Jiffy Lube) · Needs-based (most needs of one group, IKEA) · Access-based (customers reachable differently, rural cinemas).
Trade-offs = what not to do; protect the position from straddlers. Fit: 1st consistency, 2nd reinforcement, 3rd optimization of effort → the system is hard to copy.
Plan · Ploy · Pattern · Position · Perspective. Deliberate (intended & realized) vs emergent (realized without intention) vs unrealized.
Chandler: firms win through throughput and administrative coordination; structure follows strategy. Perrow: firms absorbed society and externalized costs; alternative = networks of small firms.
Martian view: large green areas (organizations), thin red lines (markets). Organizations work via authority, rewards, identification, coordination.
Persistently higher profit (or potential) than rivals in the same market. Sources: cost structure, quality, branding …

front: Why is performance hard to explain?
back: Multi-dimensional, factors hard to identify, causality hard to establish (endogeneity), model may not hold across time and places.
